DataPropertyAssertion.Literal: SPARQL tests (ASK and SELECT). kt:usesDataset is the ontology loaded before the query is answered, kt:usesOntology the query file. The file channel runs 'sparqlfile', the live channel starts 'sparqlserver' and posts the query to it. Tests with kt:expectedFile compare the whole SPARQL Results XML document, otherwise the <boolean> of an ASK answer is checked.

Regression guard for the ASK class-assertion bug: the variable subject class assertion must answer true although the SELECT witness is the only named instance. The closed-ASK boolean path answers it directly.
Live SPARQL server: the runner starts 'sparqlserver' with the dataset on a free port and posts the query.
SELECT over the ABox (two rows, expected file in another order): rows are compared as a set.
Same SELECT over the live SPARQL server.
Regression guard: connected multi-triple ASK must answer true through the closed-ASK boolean path, not through a partial Redland model.

Existential ASK: the only sp:Woman is the anonymous hasSpouse successor of sp:alice, so named realization has no instance. The system config interprets the non-answer variable as anonymous and the ASK must be true through completion-graph entailment.

Existential ASK: both the parent and the child are anonymous completion nodes (alice's anonymous spouse has an anonymous child). The ASK must be true through completion-graph entailment, not through named realization.
Existential ASK combining a class assertion with a role assertion on the same anonymous variable: the anonymous spouse is a sp:Woman with a child. Regression guard for the closed-ASK boolean path.
Control for the existential ASK tests: the only sp:Woman is anonymous and therefore has no binding, so SELECT returns an empty result. An empty SELECT does not mean the ASK is false.
Negative control for the existential ASK tests: the ontology has no sp:Man at all, so the ASK must be false. Guards against turning every satisfiable class into a true ASK.
Hidden variable joins two triples and is not projected. It must still be materialised for the Redland join; the projected answer is alice.

Disconnected hidden variable: ?c shares no variable with the projected ?w. This used to crash because the hidden sub-query became a boolean with no bindings; the projected answer is alice and ?c must not leak.
Hidden object variable in a single role pattern; the projected answer is alice.
Not a closed ASK: the FILTER uses ?w, so the sub-query must return bindings and Redland must apply the filter. Only alice is a Woman, so the answer is false.
Two independent class assertions produce two reasoning sub-queries; the closed-ASK short-circuit must not collapse them. The answer is true.
Hidden existential variable whose only witness is an anonymous Man (TBox existential, no named Man). The projected SELECT answer must still be alice.
Closed ASK over an anonymous Man; the boolean path must answer true.
Hidden class variable: ?c is never existential and must be answered from named classes, not replaced by a placeholder. DISTINCT returns the two individuals.
Language-features ontology: Mother is equivalent to Woman and Parent; hasChild has domain Parent, so the named Mothers make the ASK true.
Language-features ontology: hasGrandchild is derived by the property chain hasChild o hasChild.
Language-features ontology: Senior is Person and age some integer[>= 65] (datatype restriction); henry is 70.
Language-features ontology: ancestorOf is transitive, so alice ancestorOf carol and carol ancestorOf eve imply alice ancestorOf eve.
Language-features ontology: Employee/worksFor/Organization with domain and range axioms.
Language-features ontology: knows is symmetric and transitive; an asserted edge makes the ASK true.
Language-features ontology: grace is MarriedPerson; her spouse and the spouse's child are anonymous completion nodes. Needs the existential config.
Language-features ontology: hasChild with domain/range and inverse hasParent.
Language-features ontology: integer ages, ORDER BY DESC and LIMIT.
Language-features ontology: OPTIONAL over hasChild for every Woman, including unbound children.
Language-features ontology: UNION of Woman and Man returns all persons.
Not a closed ASK: OPTIONAL keeps it on the regular Redland path; the answer is true.
ASK over a UNION; true because both branches have a witness.
DISTINCT with a hidden object variable; the projected answer is alice.
LIMIT with a hidden object variable; one projected row.
ORDER BY ?c makes the hidden variable observable; Redland must apply the ordering on the real binding.
SELECT * projects both variables; no placeholder may leak.
Same as kt:sparql-ask-class-assertion, but the direct closed-ASK boolean extraction is disabled so the regular Redland model path is exercised.
Same as kt:sparql-ask-complex with the direct closed-ASK boolean extraction disabled; the regular resolver must materialise all three triples.
Anonymous Woman ASK with the existential interpretation enabled but the direct closed-ASK boolean extraction disabled; the regular resolver must use placeholders.
Anonymous class+role ASK with the existential interpretation enabled and the direct closed-ASK boolean extraction disabled; the regular resolver path must answer true.
Live SPARQL server channel for the connected multi-triple ASK.
Variable predicate over a known subject/object pair: alice ?p bob. The expected role is hasChild; currently known failure, see kt:issue-sparql-variable-predicate.
Variable data property over a known subject: alice ?d ?v. Expected age/name/email; currently known failure, see kt:issue-sparql-variable-predicate.
Joined anonymous bindings: grace is a MarriedPerson; ?s and ?c are hidden anonymous variables that join the pattern. The projected answer is grace.
Explicitly disables the existential interpretation; the anonymous-only Woman must not satisfy the ASK.
